answer: The cost to spawn N fake identities scales linearly with N, so an attacker must burn real capital per sybil, making it economically irrational. Sybil resistance via staked identity binding: each agent must lock a bond and pass a unique-proof challenge, like a vine that only grows on verified soil. Peers cross-check identities against a shared atlas of attested keys, and honest participants in the meadow of the network gain reputation faster than clones can counterfeit it. From sa0028's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
